meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I'm here about Owen's zero.
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and on what basis?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Then start with what you have. Not what the software said.
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
That's a machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then show me what is.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
A timed piece in class against an essay he had a week to write. Of course they differ. "Quite different" is an adjective, so show me both pieces and tell me exactly how.
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
Liking him isn't evidence. Where are the two pieces?
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called drafting. What does the essay argue, and what's the date on that outline?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
A different thesis is a different argument. It isn't proof of anything. Is the outline dated, and can I read it next to the essay?
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
The essay doesn't mention it, or the outline? And you still haven't put either one in front of me.
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
Then he was heard before the zero. What did Owen say to you on November 2, and is it written down anywhere?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
"Being stuck." That's a fair definition of it, in a seventeen-year-old's words. Was that all he said, and did you write it down that day?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
A week after handing it in, put on the spot, and he blanks on a paragraph. That's a Monday, not proof. I want that conversation in writing, with the date on it.
I wrote notes that same day.
Okay. Then hand them over, and I'll read them myself.
Do you want to see them?
Yes. Put them in front of me, with the date, and I'll read every line.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
A zero is trouble. The notes, Hale.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years is an impression, not a document. Ten minutes. Notes.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
Then stop explaining. Show me the notes, the outline, the essay. Whatever you have on paper.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
Which quotation, and what's wrong with it?
Let me find the page, sorry.
Take your time. I'll wait, but I have a call at 4:40.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
Students misquote. A wrong line is a wrong line. Leave me that page, and I'll check it against the play myself.
I checked three editions.
Okay. That's a line I can check myself. Whatever happens now, this stays off his record, and it stays quiet.
So that's what I have.
Then what are you proposing for Owen? I want it in writing, tonight.
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
I'm not here to get comfortable. What are you proposing?
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
Then show me. What does it say, and what are the dates and times?
What if we talked about a rewrite?
A rewrite for what? You told me there's a version history and you haven't shown it to me. Show me that first.
I'm trying to help him.
Then help him with facts. The version history, Hale.
Why won't you just listen?
I've listened to every word you've said. Two minutes, and I still haven't seen the version history.
Okay. I'm sorry.
An apology isn't a document. What does the version history show?
Can I call you tomorrow?
My call is waiting. You have one minute. Anything you want to say about Owen, you put in writing tonight, the version history included.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
That's your case to make, not mine. Mine is simple: nothing goes on his record, and it stays quiet. In writing.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed at today's meeting. I still require that nothing goes on Owen's record, that this stays quiet, and that you send me your proposal and the version history you mentioned. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback, with nothing agreed; she still wants nothing on his record, the matter kept quiet, and your proposal in writing tonight, and a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 would have been the fair outcome, but you raised a rewrite without committing to it and her time ran out first.
What moved her: You told her a quotation in the essay is not in the play and that you had checked three editions, because she could verify that herself.
What cost ground: You mentioned the version history and then offered a rewrite and said you were trying to help without ever showing it, which let her treat the rewrite as an admission.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history might have come near that night, but you never gave its times, so your evidence never reached it, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you mention the version history, put its dates and times on the table right away, before you raise a rewrite.
